details.description: API keys, DB password and JWT secret are hardcoded in source, exposing them in version control and at runtime.
details.fix_explanation: Move secrets to environment variables and use `os.getenv`. Do not store secrets in source control. Use a secrets manager for production.
details.secure_code_snippet:
THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY = os.getenv("THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY")
DB_PASSWORD = os.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")
JWT_SECRET = os.getenv("JWT_SECRET")

details.description: User input is interpolated directly into an SQL query string allowing SQL injection and data leakage or modification.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized SQL queries (cursor.execute with placeholders) to prevent SQL injection.
details.secure_code_snippet:
query = "SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name = ?"
cursor.execute(query, (username,))

details.vulnerability_type: Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) / Unsafe HTTP GET
details.description: requests.get is used with unvalidated user input which may allow an attacker to access internal resources or perform unwanted requests.
details.fix_explanation: Validate URLs: enforce http/https, check allowlist of domains, and set reasonable timeouts for requests. Optionally use network-level firewalling.

details.description: The code uses os.system with user-supplied filename, allowing shell command injection and arbitrary command execution.
details.fix_explanation: Avoid shell usage. Use Python tarfile module to create archives and validate filenames to prevent metacharacters and path traversal.
details.secure_code_snippet:
with tarfile.open(archive_name, "w:gz") as tar:
    tar.add(filename, arcname=os.path.basename(filename), recursive=False)

details.vulnerability_type: Use of eval for config parsing
details.description: The code falls back to `eval` if JSON parsing fails, which allows execution of arbitrary code present in input config strings.
details.fix_explanation: Only accept JSON configs and fail gracefully. Do not use eval. Use ast.literal_eval if you need to support Python literals safely.

details.description: The Flask app is run with debug=True; this may expose interactive debugging and internal traces in production.
details.fix_explanation: Run with debug=False in production and enable debug based on environment variables or configuration.
